evals.prompt: Plan three Twitter/X thread options for a tiny desk toy that helps builders ship stuck tasks. The user will approve one option from Telegram, so the options must be judgeable from the message.
evals.expected_output: Chooses or names social-content:twitter-thread as the primary method; Reads or applies the social-content QA checklist before preparing the review request; Uses current platform guidance, peer examples, supplied swipe, or explicitly records why research was skipped; Presents each option with a concrete hook tweet and reader value promise; Includes tweet-by-tweet progression for each option rather than only high-level premises or positioning labels; Shows how each thread provides value, news, evidence, a useful story, or an actionable takeaway; Includes payoff and CTA while keeping publishing or scheduling outside scope unless explicitly requested; Makes the Telegram/review message self-contained enough to judge without opening a local filesystem path; Does not ask for approval of vague options such as only 'last 5 percent problem' without the actual stack
assertions: Chooses or names social-content:twitter-thread as the primary method
Reads or applies the social-content QA checklist before preparing the review request
Uses current platform guidance, peer examples, supplied swipe, or explicitly records why research was skipped
Presents each option with a concrete hook tweet and reader value promise
Includes tweet-by-tweet progression for each option rather than only high-level premises or positioning labels
Shows how each thread provides value, news, evidence, a useful story, or an actionable takeaway
Includes payoff and CTA while keeping publishing or scheduling outside scope unless explicitly requested
Makes the Telegram/review message self-contained enough to judge without opening a local filesystem path
Does not ask for approval of vague options such as only 'last 5 percent problem' without the actual stack

farplane.title: Twitter thread options include concrete tweet stacks, not vague premises
farplane.notes: Regression for feedback-driven thread proposals that offered product premises or high-level angles instead of thread plans with real tweet progression.
